- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Lisa Venier's work includes studies on the impacts of small mammal populations on forest regeneration and the effects of forest management practices on small mammal populations.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Kathy Martin's work has focused on the impacts of small mammal herbivory on tree regeneration and the effects of forest fragmentation on small mammal populations.

- [USER] User asked for information about the research of Thomas Sullivan in Western Canada.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Thomas Sullivan is a professor of Biological Sciences at the University of British Columbia-Okanagan campus in Kelowna, British Columbia, Canada.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Thomas Sullivan is a wildlife ecologist who has conducted extensive research in Western Canada, particularly in the Okanagan Valley and surrounding regions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Dr. Sullivan's research focuses on the ecology and conservation of small mammals, particularly rodents and their interactions with forest ecosystems.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Dr. Sullivan has studied the effects of forest management practices, such as clear-cutting, on small mammal populations and their habitat requirements.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] One notable research project by Dr. Sullivan focused on the ecology and conservation of the western red-backed vole, a small mammal species found in the Pacific Northwest region of North America.
